f13.summary: Pusterla tells Sforza he has reached Gualdo and will wait at Montefiascone or Monte Guiduzo for word where to join him, with Antonio da Trezzo, and asks for a guide.

f27.summary: At Ferrara the Duca di Ferrara is suspicious for lack of news; Pusterla reassures him and urges a quick conclusion; Barbavara, going to the Pope and the King about the money, takes a copy of Pusterla's cipher.

f32.summary: A short note to the Count: no news from Sforza; Pusterla protests his loyalty and asks for instructions.

f40.summary: From Rimini: the courier is warned, a safe-conduct is sent for two of Sforza's men, and Barbavara will set out by San Giovanni in Marignano; he has dealt with Sigismondo Malatesta as instructed.

f42.summary: In Milan the Duke receives Pusterla gladly and is delighted with Sforza's disposition, but will not send him back without a good part of the money, to be collected at Ferrara.

f49.summary: In Rome Barbavara finds Eugenius IV dead; the Camerlengo will wait for the new pope and is friendly; Capua and Fermo are tipped; a show of force in the Marche would loosen the cardinals' purses.

f56.summary: King Alfonso agrees to pay Sforza's condotta, 94,000 ducats a year for two years, on a schedule that includes 20,000 owed by the Duca di Ferrara, which the King will make him pay.

f62.summary: The cardinals have entered the conclave; letters go by Madonna Aura and Messer Angelo in Urbino; Alfonso's letters enclosed, the King pleased that Sforza has turned from the Kingdom.

f69.summary: The new pope is proclaimed at about the seventeenth hour: Tommaso Parentucelli, Nicholas V ("Monsignore da Cologna" in the copy, for Bologna).

f67.summary: Pusterla presses the Duca di Ferrara to help the Duke of Milan, with little hope, and complains of no answers since Reggio.

f71.summary: The Duca di Ferrara says his revenues cannot bear the cost of lord Guidemo's troops, but offers to join the war against Venice on terms he once proposed; three briefs enclosed.

f75.summary: Barbavara at the new pope's feet; the pope sends the Camerlengo and the Vice-Chancellor to Alfonso about peace in Italy; the King says priests are men "da bastonate, non da pregare".

f77.summary: Twenty thousand ducats wait at Ferrara for Sforza's messenger; the Venetian army came to Cremona crying "viva San Marco", but the town held for Sforza.

f81.summary: The Venetians have moved on Soncino; the Count of Urbino is negotiating; the Duca di Ferrara is heartened by Nicholas V's election; a Venetian hope of Cremona through a squad captain.

f135.summary: From what the Duke writes about Roberto da Montalboddo and what he has heard from the King, Barbavara thinks his staying in Rome is no longer needed, and asks Sforza to say so at once.

f143.summary: The Malatesta coming over to the King, the bulls for their vicariates, the new pope stalling until the outcome is settled, and 4,000 ducats agreed with the Count of Urbino's ambassadors.

snip.cap: Barbavara, Rome, 6 March 1447: the cipher slip announcing the new pope
